significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish the form-(iii) law that knowledge type follows a reproducible "localization spectrum"—factual knowledge being mid-layer/MLP-localized, conceptual and relational knowledge more attention-distributed, and procedural knowledge later and serial—and that position on this spectrum predicts editing success, paraphrase robustness, and stored-but-unretrieved failures. This would establish both a mechanistic ordering and behavioral predictive couplings, constraining where retrieval should peak and which knowledge classes should be editable or retrieval-fragile; that directly bears on the unresolved localization-to-editability link highlighted by Hase et al.'s "Does Localization Inform Editing?" and on the factual-recall mechanisms characterized by Geva et al. (EMNLP 2023). The claim is determinate, and its negative branch is also informative: failure of a stable ordering or of the three predicted couplings would rule out knowledge-type geometry as a general explanation rather than merely failing to find one component. Topic substitution fails—the generic assigned topic would not itself imply this four-way ordering and multi-outcome predictive law—so the score reflects the claim-specific increment.

reach.justification: The claim names reusable handles—"LocalizationScore," "MLP-Attention reliance ratio," "PeakLayerDepth," and "MechanismParaphraseInvariance"—and proposes the localization spectrum itself as a predictor of "where editing works" and "when stored knowledge fails to surface." These are partly ex ante handles: after measuring a knowledge class, an editor or auditor could anticipate editability, paraphrase fragility, or retrieval failure before applying an edit or relying on answers, rather than merely explaining an observed error post hoc. Because the asserted conclusion is an ordering and predictive coupling across knowledge types, re-extraction on another model would test predicted ranks and relationships rather than merely initiate an unconstrained search; its stated scope spans model families and scales, with downstream use by knowledge editors and model auditors, although it does not itself supply a deployment-ready gate or reach outside AI. Topic substitution again fails because the topic alone supplies neither these quantitative handles nor the transferable ordering, supporting reach above the topic-median probe-and-steer result.
